summary: Tower on Jesmond Mountain, staffed 1972 to 1999; destroyed by wildfire in July 2026, with only its base reported left.

facts.design: Tower tied to the bedrock with metal cables
facts.status_note: Destroyed by wildfire in July 2026; a 2026 newspaper reports only the tower's base was left.

access.note: In an August 2026 statement quoted by the Four Wheel Drive Association of BC, Recreation Sites and Trails BC said the site remained closed.

events.note: Register gives 1971; a 2026 newspaper says built in the early 1970s.
Observers stationed in fire season, three weeks at a time.
Staffed through 1999, per the register and the visitor account.

Register: destroyed by the Fiftynine Creek Fire on 17 July 2026. Free Press: destroyed in the Pear Lake wildfire. Four Wheel Drive Association: lost in the Big Bar Complex wildfires. Loss confirmed 27 July.
Site closed for active wildfire, an evacuation order and safety hazards; still closed in the August 2026 statement.
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register as CAN 3, BC 1, dated 11 October 2026.

notes_for_editor: Fire name differs across sources: register says Fiftynine Creek Fire on 17 July 2026; Free Press says Pear Lake wildfire; Four Wheel Drive Association says Big Bar Complex. All three are reported in the story; both later reports agree the loss was confirmed 27 July. Elevation: register 1,959 m, Free Press 1,980 m, visitor account 1,970 m (not cited in story); firelookout.ca gives 1908 m (not cited). The RSTBC resource page (sitesandtrailsbc.ca/resource/REC205666) returned no text to fetch_text; a search snippet from it says the tower was built about 1972, which differs from the register's 1971; not used. Newest source found is the 13 Aug 2026 Free Press piece; current site status after that is not known. Brief access 'unknown' changed to closed per the August 2026 statement. Record status gone and agency match the sources.
